author: edward841
body: Implemented a working finite state machine (FSM) for the game. This acts as the skeleton that provides overarching structure for the rest of the game. It focuses on specifying the macro structure of the game (there are 6 rounds, each has 3 phases, that happen in this order). It specifies when players get a turn, and I also implemented variable turn order. At the moment the only action a player can do is pass (but there is groundwork laid for other actions when they are implemented).

body:
This branch add three features(State, `fixCars`, `CarLog`) and some changes in `struct Car` in `CarRental.sol`
1. Add 2 states (Available, Unavailable) for `Car` in the contract to replace `isDamaged` and `isRented`. Both of them are considered as `Unavailable` and vice versa.
2. Change `rentalAddress` to `user`. 
    - When a car is new added, its `user` is assigned to the `owner`.  
    - When a car is rented, its `user` is changed to the renter(`msg.sender`).
    -  When a rented car is returned, its `user` is changed back to the `owner`. 
3. If the `state` is `Unavailable` and the `user` is `owner`, it means the car is damaged.
4. The `fixCars` function is declared `onlyOwner`. It is used to fix all damaged cars.
5. The `CarLog` event is emitted when the car is damaged and fixed.

body:
This PR covers changes which simplify the use of the `DataSource` class for:
1. Users writing programs (especially with validation data), and
2. The internal management of `DataSource`s in PZ

The primary changes I made were to:
1. Reduce the three data source classes (`DataSource`, `AbstractDataSource`, and `ValidationDataSource`) down to a single `DataSource` class
2. Limit the number of methods the user needs to implement to just `__len__()` and `get_item()`

This in turn led to a number of other changes / simplifications in the code including:
1. Using `datasource` directly in the scan operators (both logical and physical) instead of `dataset_id`
2. Changing `source_id` --> `source_idx` everywhere (this eliminated some weird renaming logic)
3. And various other small fixes which resulted from these changes

Finally, I added a large set of documentation for the `DataSource` class(es)

## Why am I making these changes?
[editorconfig](https://editorconfig.org/) is a standard used by many open source libraries that keeps coding style standardized. Editors and auto formatting tools will respect this. It is also meant to be committed to the repository.
It's annoying to write in this codebase without there being an .editorconfig file, as every time you make a new file, or add a newline, etc., the auto formatter will not respect the project's style.

## What are the changes from a developer perspective?
Developers using a code editor that supports `.editorconfig` (nearly all do) will now have defaults added.
For example, when editing a file in vscode, pressing newline or tab will no longer tab to 4 characters, and will instead tab to the 2 characters as is done in this codebase.
